response.original_text: "ANG GALING NI SEC. VINCE" Muling nabuksan ang usapin sa kalidad ng EDSA rehabilitation project matapos maiulat na ilang bahagi ng kalsadang isinailalim sa road reblocking ay nagkaroon na agad ng mga lubak at pagkabakbak sa kabila ng kamakailang pagkakagawa nito. Batay sa ulat ng 24 Oras, kabilang sa mga apektadong lugar ang ilang seksyon ng EDSA Busway at mga bahagi ng Phase 1 ng road reblocking project na sinimulan noong bisperas ng Pasko noong nakaraang taon. Tinatayang aabot sa P1.2 bilyon ang halaga ng naturang proyekto. Dahil dito, binatikos ni veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza ang Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) sa ilalim ni Secretary Vince Dizon. Sa kanyang social media post, kinuwestiyon niya kung bakit nagkaroon agad ng sira ang ilang bahagi ng EDSA sa kabila ng malaking pondong inilaan para sa rehabilitasyon. Sa ngayon, wala pang inilalabas na pahayag si Dizon kaugnay sa mga batikos at sa ulat hinggil sa kondisyon ng ilang bagong inayos na bahagi ng pangunahing lansangan sa Metro Manila.

citations.quote: Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon on Monday blamed concrete barriers along the EDSA Busway for potholes that developed on the southbound portion of the newly rehabilitated highway near Buendia, saying the barriers prevented rainwater from properly draining.
At a Palace briefing, Dizon said he was furious after inspecting a portion of the newly rehabilitated EDSA over the weekend amid heavy rains and finding potholes caused by damaged asphalt.
“Ang damaged area doon sa catch basin between Estrella and Buendia.
Doon kasi ang bagsak ng lahat ng tubig mula Guadalupe pababa.
Makikita ninyo naman eh, doon talaga ang bagsak.
So ang problema lang doon, ‘yung mga barrier ng busway,” Dizon said.
(The damaged area is at the catch basin between Estrella and Buendia.
That’s where all the water flowing down from Guadalupe collects.
You can see it for yourselves.
The problem there is the busway barriers.) Dizon explained that the busway barriers prevented rainwater from reaching the drainage system, causing water to accumulate and damage the asphalt.
“Hinaharang ‘yung pag-drain ng tubig mula sa busway, papunta sa drainage natin sa kabilang side.
So, kung mapapansin ninyo ‘yung area na ‘yun, ‘yung area na nakakalabas ang tubig walang sira.
Pero ‘yung area sa busway na ang tubig naiiwan dahil nakaharang ‘yung mga barrier ng busway,” he added.
(The barriers are preventing water from the busway from flowing into the drainage system on the other side.
If you look at the area, the section where water can drain properly is undamaged.

But the section along the busway, where water accumulates because the barriers block its flow, is damaged.) Dizon said he had spoken with the Department of Transportation (DOTr) and the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) about rearranging the concrete barriers along the EDSA Busway and leaving gaps between them to allow water to flow into the drainage system.
“Kasi ang number one na kalaban ng aspalto eh tubig.
Kapag ang tubig naiwan kahit na ilang oras lang iyan, ito araw ang binilang, talagang masisira ‘yun,” he explained.
(The number one enemy of asphalt is water.

If water is left standing for even just a few hours—let alone for days—it will really cause damage.) Forbes Park wall Dizon also said authorities should determine who was responsible for building the perimeter wall of North Forbes Park in Makati City that collapsed over the weekend.
“Clearly, hindi maayos ‘yung pagkagawa noong perimeter wall ng North Forbes Park,” he said.

(Clearly, the North Forbes Park perimeter wall was not properly constructed.) “Ngayon, ang kailangan nating malaman since matagal na ‘yan, tingin ko medyo dekada na rin ‘yung binilang ng mga pader na ‘yan, we have to find out muna sino ba ang gumawa, sino ba ang nagpagawa nito,” he continued.

(Now, what we need to determine, since those walls have been there for quite some time—probably for decades—is who built them and who commissioned their construction.) The DPWH chief said the agency is seeking the MMDA’s assistance in identifying those responsible for the collapsed wall so they can be held accountable.
“And number two, we have to decide kung ano ang gagawin doon, gigibain na ba ‘yun nang safely?
So makikipag-coordinate tayo sa LGU at sa MMDA kung ano ang gagawin natin doon, pero definitely, kailangang ayusin na ‘yun,” he said.
(Secondly, we have to decide what to do with it and whether it needs to be safely demolished.
We will coordinate with the local government and the MMDA on the next steps, but it definitely needs to be fixed.) — MCG GMA News

citations.quote: Commuters may expect wider sidewalks and motorists will have a smoother ride throughout EDSA once its rehabilitation is finished by next year, Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon said Monday.
"Buong stretch ng EDSA mula south hanggang Monumento lalaparan natin 'yung sidewalk para sa mga kababayan natin," Dizon said in an interview on Unang Balita after inspecting the EDSA-Buendia area.

(On the whole stretch of EDSA from the south until Monumento, we will widen the sidewalk for our countrymen.) He also said the asphalt being used on EDSA is of good quality, at par with that being used in other countries like Japan and Korea.

"Ongoing ang Phase 2 (ng EDSA rehabilitation) mula Guadalupe Orense hanggang Monumento. Ngayon nagtatrabaho tayo sa Monumento side. Kanina ininspeksiyon ko 'yung bandang Boni papunta ng Shaw Boulevard, nag-aayos na rin tayo diyan. By next year, tingin ko, tapos na ito," Dizon said.
(Phase 2 [of EDSA rehabilitation] from Guadalupe Orense to Monumento is ongoing.
We are working on the Monumento side.
Earlier, I inspected the area [of EDSA] from Boni [Avenue] toward Shaw Boulevard as we are working there too.

By next year, I think we will be finished.) Sidewalks Dizon said he walked on EDSA near Buendia with Transportation Secretary Giovanni "Banoy" Lopez last year and saw for themselves how narrow the sidewalk was for commuters to walk on.

"Last year naglakad kami dito with Sec. Banoy and nakita natin na kawawa talaga 'yung mga kababayan natin na nagco-commute at saka ang mga naglalakad. Kasi maraming, lingid sa kaalaman ng mga kababayan nating motorista, ang daming naglalakad sa EDSA eh. Ang problema, walang lalakaran," he said.
(Last year, Sec. Banoy and I walked here and we saw that our commuters are having a hard time walking here.
Motorists may not know this, but there are many who walk on EDSA.

The problem is, there is no adequate walkway.) "Dito lang sa area na ito dito sa Buendia Station, halos wala na 'yan eh. Kung bumaba ka ng Buendia MRT, baba ka dito, wala kang .. Halos dinoble natin 'yung lawak (ng sidewalk) para may lalakaran 'yung mga kababayan natin," Dizon said.
(For instance, here at Buendia Station area.
There is hardly any sidewalk.
If you down from the Buendia MRT and go down here, there is not enough space for you to walk on...

We doubled the sidewalk area so our countrymen will have enough space to walk on.) "Pati siklista natin puwedeng dito na rin mag-bike para hindi na rin sila delikado sa mga motor at saka mga sasakyan," he said.

(Even cyclists, they can bike here on the sidewalk, and that would be safer for them away from motorcycles and motorists.) "Pati itong sidewalk, ang buong EDSA kung ano ang nakikita ng mga kababayan natin dito ngayon, ganito ang magiging sidewalk ng buong EDSA," Dizon said.

(What you see here now on this sidewalk, this is what sidewalks on the entire EDSA would look like.) Asphalt on road Dizon also said they want to ensure that motorists will be able to travel faster on EDSA via the use of high quality asphalt for overlay and improvement of the drainage system.
"Unang una, de kalidad na aspalto ang ginagamit natin, 'yung matibay kamukha nang ginagamit ng mas mayayamang bansa tulad ng Japan ng Korea. 'Yun na 'yung ni-require natin na standard dito," he said.
(First, we are using high quality asphalt, the sturdy one like that being used by more prosperous countries like Japan and Korea.

That's what we required as standard.) "Ikalawa, ang kalaban kasi ng aspalto, tubig. Itong mga inlet, basta 'yung pasukan ng tubig, maliliit kasi 'yung mga inlet dito sa EDSA at sa mga ibang national road natin. Ang gagawin natin, dodoblehin, titriplehin natin para 'yung kunyari magka-flash flood o malakas na ulan, mabilis na malalabas papasok sa drainage. Hindi masyadong masisira nang mabilis 'yung ating aspalto," Dizon said.
(Second, water destroys asphalt.
The inlets here on EDSA and other national roads are small.
What we will do is double, triple these so that in case there is flash flood or heavy rain, the water will go to the drainage faster.

The asphalt will not be damaged as fast as before.) "So 'yung mga 'yon ginagawa natin para talagang tumagal ang aspaltong nilalagay natin. Mas maginhawa ang biyahe. Mas mabilis din. Bibilis 'yan kasi dati lubak-lubak," he added.
(So that's what we will do to make the asphalt last longer.
As a result, motorists will have a smoother ride, a faster one since there won't be any potholes anymore.) Mass transport Dizon also said to decongest EDSA, mass transport has to be improved.

"Ang importante talaga, ang makakapagpaluwag sa EDSA, 'yung mass transport. So kailangan talagang padamihin ang bus sa busway natin, padamihin ang tren natin sa MRT na kaya naman gawin ng DOTr (Department of Transportation) at gagawin naman," he said.
(What's important and what will help decongest EDSA is the mass transport.

So we need to add more buses to the busway and more trains to the MRT, which the DOTr can do and will do.) "Importante din 'yung motorista natin, kombinyente ang biyahe niya at maiiwasan natin 'yung pagtagal ng tubig at 'yung pagbaba," Dizon said.

(It's also important so motorists can experience convenience in traveling and we can avoid the slow drainage of water.) Infra projects full speed ahead corruption-free The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) secretary then assured the public that infrastructure projects will now be on full speed ahead with no trace of corruption.
"Rarantsada na tayo (we'll go on full speed ahead)," Dizon said.

"Ang nangyari talaga diyan, nu'ng nakaraang mga taon at dekada, naglalagay ng proyekto sa budget, nagpapa-bid ng proyekto na walang papeles. 'Di ba nakita nga natin noong nag-iinspeksyon tayo ng mga maanomalyang flood control, naghahanap ng plano si presidente, walang mai-produce na plano. Kasi nga hindi ganu'n ang ginagawa eh," he said.
(What happened before, in the past years and decades, allocations for funds for projects were included in the budget and bidding activities were done without the adequate documents.
Isn't it when we inspected anomalous flood control projects before, the president was looking for plans?

No plan could be produced because there wasn't any.) "Isipin mo, gagawa ka ng proyekto, magpapa-bid ka, walang plano. Ngayon hindi na pupuwede 'yon. Sabi ng pangulo natin, kailangan lahat ng required documents, lahat ng mga plano, kompleto," Dizon said.
(Imagine that, you will do a project and call for a bidding without a plan.
That is not allowed anymore.

Our president said all required documents, plans should be complete.) "'Yon, siyempre may oras na kasama 'yon. Pero masisigurado natin ngayon na maayos ang pagbi-bid natin, maayos ang budgeting. Pero 'yan, natapos na 'yan lahat. Ngayon, ratsada na, tuloy-tuloy na tayo," he said.
(Of course that would take time.
But we can assure the public now that the bidding is above board, and so is the budgeting.
So we finished all that.

Now we can go full speed ahead.) "'Yan po ang maa-assure natin sa mga kababayan natin (na walang corruption) kasi talagang binabantayan natin at makikita nila sa trabaho. Ngayon, makikita natin," Dizon said.

(That's what we can assure the public, that there is no corruption because we are closely monitoring this and you can see that in the result.) The DPWH official cited the drainage and flood control project on G. Araneta Avenue in Quezon City which has helped lessen the extent of flooding in the area.
"Halimbawa 'no, 'yung mga inayos nating mga drainage at flood control sa G. Araneta.
Ang mga kababayan mismo natin na ang nagsasabi na konti na lang ang pagbaha doon.

Eh dati hanggang lampas tao diyan," Dizon said. (For instance, we fixed the drainage and flood control on G. Araneta. The people themselves are the ones saying that the flooding now is lesser as compared before. Floodwaters would reach over an average man's height before.) "So ganu'ng klase ang mga proyekto na gustong mangyari ng ating pangulo na kapag, sabi nga niya, kapag ginamit nang tama at hindi ninanakaw ang pondo, nagbebenepisyo talaga ang mga kababayan natin," he added.
(So that's the kind of projects our president wants, wherein if funds are used well and not stolen, it's the public that would benefit.) —KG GMA News

content_profile.verification_text:
"ANG GALING NI SEC. VINCE"
Muling nabuksan ang usapin sa kalidad ng EDSA rehabilitation project matapos maiulat na ilang bahagi ng kalsadang isinailalim sa road reblocking ay nagkaroon na agad ng mga lubak at pagkabakbak sa kabila ng kamakailang pagkakagawa nito.
Batay sa ulat ng 24 Oras, kabilang sa mga apektadong lugar ang ilang seksyon ng EDSA Busway at mga bahagi ng Phase 1 ng road reblocking project na sinimulan noong bisperas ng Pasko noong nakaraang taon.
Tinatayang aabot sa P1.2 bilyon ang halaga ng naturang proyekto.
Dahil dito, binatikos ni veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza ang Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) sa ilalim ni Secretary Vince Dizon.
Sa kanyang social media post, kinuwestiyon niya kung bakit nagkaroon agad ng sira ang ilang bahagi ng EDSA sa kabila ng malaking pondong inilaan para sa rehabilitasyon.
Sa ngayon, wala pang inilalabas na pahayag si Dizon kaugnay sa mga batikos at sa ulat hinggil sa kondisyon ng ilang bagong inayos na bahagi ng pangunahing lansangan sa Metro Manila.
content_profile.normalized_verification_text:
"SEC. VINCE IS GREAT"
The issue regarding the quality of the EDSA rehabilitation project has resurfaced after it was reported that some parts of the road subjected to road reblocking developed potholes and peeling despite the recent completion of the work.
According to a report by 24 Oras, among the affected areas are several sections of the EDSA Busway and parts of Phase 1 of the road reblocking project that began on Christmas Eve of last year.
The estimated cost of the project is about P1.2 billion.
As a result, veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza criticized the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) under Secretary Vince Dizon.
In his social media post, he questioned why there were already damages in some parts of EDSA despite the large funds allocated for the rehabilitation.
As of now, Dizon has not released any statements regarding the criticisms and the report concerning the condition of some newly repaired sections of the main thoroughfare in Metro Manila.

claims.evidence_context:
"SEC. VINCE IS GREAT"
The issue regarding the quality of the EDSA rehabilitation project has resurfaced after it was reported that some parts of the road subjected to road reblocking developed potholes and peeling despite the recent completion of the work.
According to a report by 24 Oras, among the affected areas are several sections of the EDSA Busway and parts of Phase 1 of the road reblocking project that began on Christmas Eve of last year.
The estimated cost of the project is about P1.2 billion.
As a result, veteran broadcaster Jay Sonza criticized the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) under Secretary Vince Dizon.
In his social media post, he questioned why there were already damages in some parts of EDSA despite the large funds allocated for the rehabilitation.
As of now, Dizon has not released any statements regarding the criticisms and the report concerning the condition of some newly repaired sections of the main thoroughfare in Metro Manila.
